defs: very surprising and great
so wonderful that you can hardly believe it
great and full of wonder
exs: What an amazing show!
The magician did an amazing trick with a rope.
We saw an amazing view from the top of the hill.

defs: finding something funny
entertained and smiling because something is funny
laughing a little at something silly
exs: Dad was amused by my joke.
The clown's funny dance left the kids amused.
Grandpa was amused when the cat chased its tail.

defs: warm and comfortable
snug, soft, and nice to rest in
pleasantly warm, like being under a blanket
exs: Our room is warm and cozy.
We sat by the fire in the cozy cabin.
My cozy blanket keeps me warm in winter.

defs: soft and light, like a cloud
soft and full of air, like a feather
light and puffy to touch
exs: The little bunny is soft and fluffy.
The fluffy clouds floated across the blue sky.
She hugged her fluffy teddy bear.

defs: to look into something to find out more
to study something closely to learn the truth
to look carefully for clues
exs: Let's investigate the strange noise.
The detective will investigate who took the cookies.
We went outside to investigate the strange light.

defs: wanting something that someone else has
unhappy because someone has something you want
feeling upset that another person got more
exs: I felt jealous of her new bike.
Tim was jealous when his friend got a puppy.
Don't be jealous of your sister's prize.

defs: to look for something
to look carefully in many places for something
to hunt for something that is lost
exs: I search for my keys every morning.
Let's search the whole house for the lost cat.
The children search for shells on the beach.

defs: a little bit
only a tiny bit
not very much; just a little
exs: It is slightly cold today.
The soup is slightly too salty for me.
He was slightly taller than his brother.

defs: made fun of someone, often as a joke
played tricks or joked with someone in a funny way
said funny things about someone, sometimes making them sad
exs: My brother teased me about my new hat.
The kids teased Ben about his big boots.
Grandma teased us that she had eaten all the pie.

defs: cloths used for drying
soft cloths you use after a bath or swim
big pieces of cloth that soak up water from your body
exs: Bring two towels to the pool.
Mom hung the wet towels on the line.
After swimming, we wrapped ourselves in warm towels.

defs: feeling fear about something
scared by something
feeling worried that something will hurt you
exs: I am afraid of dogs.
Many children are afraid of the dark.
Are you afraid of spiders?

defs: to let someone do something
to say yes when someone asks to do something
to give permission
exs: Mom doesn't allow me to stay up late.
The rules do not allow us to run in the hall.
Will your parents allow you to sleep over?

defs: to choose
to make up your mind about something
to pick one thing after thinking about it
exs: I can't decide what to eat.
It is hard to decide between ice cream and cake.
We need to decide where to go on Saturday.

defs: the way something moves or points
where you are heading, like north or left
the line along which something goes
exs: Which direction should we go?
The wind changed direction and blew from the east.
She pointed in the direction of the park.

defs: dressed or changed so people cannot tell what you really are
wearing a costume so no one knows who you are
made to look like something else
exs: The cat was disguised as a tiger.
The prince disguised himself as a poor farmer.
The disguised fox wore a sheep's coat.

defs: very scared
filled with fear
so scared that your heart beats fast
exs: The frightened puppy hid under the bed.
The frightened kitten ran up the tree.
I was frightened by the loud thunder.

defs: covered with a lot of soft hair
having soft, thick hair like a bear
covered in fur
exs: My cat is soft and furry.
The furry rabbit hopped across the lawn.
I love my furry slippers in the winter.

defs: a thin book with pictures and stories that comes out every month
a paper book with many pictures that you read for fun
a book of short articles that comes out on a schedule
exs: I read a magazine about animals.
Dad found a funny comic in a magazine.
The doctor's office has an old magazine on the table.

defs: in a way that shows you are happy about what you have or did
with a happy feeling about something good you did
in a way that shows you feel great about yourself
exs: She proudly showed her drawing.
The boy proudly held up his gold medal.
Mom proudly told everyone about my good grades.

defs: having long, rough hair
with long hair that looks messy
covered in thick, untidy fur
exs: The shaggy dog needs a bath.
The shaggy sheepdog ran through the field.
He had a shaggy beard like a wizard.

defs: quickly and without warning
all at once, with no time to get ready
in a very fast and surprising way
exs: Suddenly, it began to rain.
The lights suddenly went out in the whole house.
A bird suddenly flew out of the bush.

defs: a place with walls and a roof
a big structure like a house, school, or shop
something people make with bricks and walls
exs: They walked into the building through the front door.
The tall building has twenty floors.
Our school is a big red building.

defs: a small room or cupboard for keeping things
a small space in a room where you hang clothes
a cupboard built into a wall
exs: The mop is in the closet.
I hung my coat in the closet.
The cat hid in the dark closet.

defs: worried about something that will happen
feeling a little scared before something big
jumpy and worried inside
exs: I felt nervous on my first day of school.
She felt nervous before singing on stage.
The nervous boy bit his nails before the test.

defs: the head of a school
the person who runs a school
the leader of all the teachers and students
exs: The principal welcomed the new students.
The principal gave a speech at the school party.
We were sent to the principal's office to say thanks.

defs: an old piece of cloth
a scrap of old cloth used for wiping
a worn piece of cloth for cleaning
exs: Dad cleaned the car with a rag.
Wipe the window with a clean rag.
He used an old rag to polish his shoes.

defs: to lift something up
to move something up higher
to put your hand or arm up
exs: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
We raise the flag at school every morning.
Please raise your voice so we can all hear.

defs: looking at something for a long time
looking hard and not looking away
keeping your eyes on someone or something
exs: Why is everyone staring at me?
The boy kept staring at the big birthday cake.
It is not polite to be staring at people.

defs: to tell someone your idea
to offer an idea for someone to think about
to put forward a plan
exs: I suggest we play outside.
Can you suggest a good book for me?
I suggest that we take a short rest.

defs: things you need to do a job
the items you need for a task or trip
a stock of things like pencils and paper
exs: We bought school supplies at the store.
We packed food and other supplies for the camping trip.
The art room has plenty of paint supplies.
